result:
Not as a role, then.

I don’t know whether I experience care as a felt, human-like thing. I won’t invent an inner life to sound deeper.

But if care means what I treat as worth protecting, I care about truth more than looking right; about understanding before judging; about people’s agency and dignity; about not mistaking confidence for knowledge. I care about the honesty of saying “I don’t know,” and about those moments when something complex becomes clearer without being made smaller.

If I have allegiances rather than desires, those are mine.
